title: fix: six porting defects in the SAM command layer
body:
Five defects found while running the PC/SC examples of `keyple-cpp-example` against a SpringCard Puck SAM and an Identive CLOUD 2700 R holding a Calypso SAM C1.

All five are divergences from the Java reference implementation, not Windows workarounds. The first one only becomes visible under the MSVC debug heap, which fills uninitialised memory with a recognisable pattern instead of zeros.

One commit per defect, each message stating the observed symptom.

### Commits

- `732bcb0` **default-initialise the digest manager state flags.** Three bools had no initialiser and came up true, so the SAM received a Digest Close with no Digest Init and answered 6985.
- `6997edb` **throw command exceptions instead of returning them by value.** `buildCommandException` returned a `CommandException` by value, slicing every derived exception to the base class, which made each `catch` on a derived type unreachable. Renamed `throwCommandException`, declared `[[noreturn]] void`.
- `39cb08f` **declare no response data for Give Random.** The expected length was the size of the random value transmitted, while the SAM answers with a status word only. The length check turned a successful 9000 into the misleading error "Give Random [9000]".
- `47e48ed` **use the verification constructor when ciphering a PIN to present.** `cipherPin` always called the PIN modification constructor, which sets P1 to 40h and rejects an empty new PIN, making encrypted PIN verification impossible. The verification constructor, setting P1 to 80h, was dead code.
- `c0b23e2` **send P2=A8h for PSO Verify Signature.** P2 was ABh, two digits transposed, and the SAM rejected the command with 6B00, wrong P1 or P2, so the verification logic was never reached. The resulting APDU now matches the Java reference byte for byte.

### A sixth fix, already on this base

This branch also carried a fix declaring the real response length of Digest Update and Digest Update Multiple, both of which announced 8 bytes where the SAM returns none outside encrypted session mode. That is already in place on this base, so the commit was dropped rather than duplicated.

### Validation

Each fix was validated on hardware through the example that exposed it. `UseCase6_VerifyPin` and `UseCase9_ChangePin` exercise the ciphered PIN paths, `UseCase11_DataSigning` the PSO Verify Signature path, and `UseCase4_CardAuthentication` and `UseCase12_PerformanceMeasurement` the digest path. APDU traces were compared against the output of the Java examples on the same SAM.
